title: Selective synthesis of dense high-spin D1 active sites via engineered less-graphitized carbon environments
content:
Energy Environ. Sci., 2025, Advance Article
DOI: 10.1039/D5EE00141B, Paper
Xuan Luo, Jia-Bao Nie, Huang Liang, Yu-Yang Li, You-Heng Wang, Qi-Kang Que, Jean-Pol Dodelet, Yu-Cheng Wang
Introducing ascorbic acid in the synthesis of Fe–N–C catalysts drastically increases its D1 active site content, improving the cathodic activity of Fe–N–C, but also reducing the stability of the catalyst in proton exchange membrane fuel cells.
